messages.subject: predict vs backtransform
parts:
Hello! I am relatively new to occupancy modeling and the Unmarked package, and would appreciate a little clarification about how to generate p and psi estimates


We surveyed for salamanders using traditional survey methods in an occupancy framework. We also collected eDNA samples during one of three traditional surveys. Three individual eDNA samples were collected 30 minutes apart from each other. We therefore wanted to analyze the eDNA data using an occupancy framework as well. We would like to investigate the utility of eDNA (i.e. occupancy and detection estimates), as well as the factors that influence eDNA detection.

We have two questions about this:


1)     1) Because eDNA samples were taken on the same day, the covariates of detection do not change between surveys (e.g. number of days since last rainfall, turtle density at site, water temperature). Does this violate assumptions of the occupancy framework?

2)    2)  How should occupancy and detection estimates be derived when covariates are present in the model? How are the two methods below different from one another?

 

1)     Predict

              newdata <- data.frame(covariate1 = seq(min,max, length.out=100), covariate2 = seq(min, max, length.out=100))

 

              predict(mod, type="det", newdata=newdata)

              predict(mod, type="state", newdata=newdata)

 

              #take average of each output

 

2)     Backtransform

             backTransform(linearComb(mod, coefficients = c(mean, mean), type = 'det'))

             backTransform(linearComb(mod, coefficients = c(mean, mean), type = 'state'))

messages.author: 00ebeb6e0521112d
messages.subject: AW: [unmarked] predict vs backtransform
parts:
Hi unknown person,

 

I think that having identical covariate values doesn’t invalidate use of your model in the least. And predict and backTransform are in part functionally synonymous, but I think the former is more general. I always use predict and never the latter.

 

Best regards  ---- Marc
